text:
Predicates:
Schedule(x) ::: x schedules a meeting with their customers.
GoToBuilding(x) ::: x will go to the company building today.
LunchInBuilding(x) ::: x has lunch in the company building.
LunchAtHome(x) ::: x has lunch at home.
WorkRemotely(x) ::: x is working remotely from home.
InOtherCountries(x) ::: x is in other countries.
Manager(x) ::: x is a manager.
Premises:
∀x (Schedule(x) → GoToBuilding(x)) ::: All employees who schedule a meeting with their customers will go to the company building today.
∀x (LunchInBuilding(x) → Schedule(x)) ::: Everyone who has lunch in the company building schedules meetings with their customers.
∀x (LunchInBuilding(x) ⊕ LunchAtHome(x)) ::: Employees have lunch either in the company building or at home.
∀x (LunchAtHome(x) → WorkRemotely(x)) ::: If an employee has lunch at home, they are working remotely from home.
∀x (InOtherCountries(x) → WorkRemotely(x)) ::: All employees who are in other countries work remotely from home.
∀x (Manager(x) → ¬WorkRemotely(x)) ::: No managers work remotely from home.
GoToBuilding(james) ↔ Manager(x) ::: James will appear in the company today if and only if he is a manager.
Conclusion:
(Manager(james) ∨ InOtherCountries(james)) → ¬(LunchAtHome(james) ∨ WorkRemotely(james)) ::: If James is either a manager or in other countries, then James does not either have lunch at home or work remotely from home.
(LunchAtHome(james) ∨ WorkRemotely(james)) → ¬(Manager(james) ∨ InOtherCountries(james)) ::: If James either has lunch at home or works remotely from home, then he is neither a manager nor does he work in other countries.
